widgets_values:
## 2 · Models
Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 + Lightning LoRA (4 steps, cfg 1). For maximum quality bypass the Lightning LoRA and set every KSampler to **steps 40 / cfg 4**.

Uses the INT8 ConvRot weights (19 GB). Best quality on a 32 GB+ GPU: pick `qwen_image_edit_2511_bf16.safetensors` in the UNETLoader (38 GB; StandRig Setup can download and switch it).

The Multiple-Angles LoRA (fal) is only used by the turnaround sheet; StandRig targets use exact-degree instructions on the base model.

## 1 · Input
Load **one** picture of your character (full body, front facing works best).

* Background is removed with BiRefNet and the character is centred on a white canvas.
* `Normalize pose` (optional, off by default): Qwen-Image-Edit redraws the character front-facing, eyes open, mouth closed, arms slightly away from the body — the pose Live2D/StandRig rigs need. Turn it on when your picture is a dynamic pose or 3/4 view.
* Everything downstream uses the **source canvas** from `StandRig Prepare Canvas`.

Redraw the character as a clean character model reference for Live2D rigging: full body, standing straight and facing the viewer directly, head level and looking at the viewer, eyes fully open, mouth closed in a neutral expression, arms relaxed and held slightly away from the torso so the sides of the body are visible, legs slightly apart, no props in the hands, nothing overlapping the face. Keep exactly the same character: same face, eye shape and eye color, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, accessories, line-art thickness, cel-shading style, color palette and lighting. Keep the same canvas size, framing and scale, and a plain flat white background. Do not add new objects, text, effects or shadows on the background.
nodes.title: Normalize-pose prompt

widgets_values:
## 4 · Face targets (StandRig contract)
Panels: neutral, yaw-min/max, pitch-min/max, roll-min/max on the face close-up.

* yaw/pitch are AI edits with exact-degree instructions (defaults ±30° / ±20°).
* roll is an **exact rotation** of the approved neutral art around the chin/neck pivot, so it never drifts off-model. Set `roll_mode` = ai to generate it instead.
* Directions are written from the viewer's side in the manifest (`direction`).
eyes-closed, eyes-smile, mouth-a, mouth-i, mouth-u, mouth-e, mouth-o, brows-angry, brows-sad
nodes.title: Prompts · face_targets

widgets_values:
## 5 · Body targets
neutral, body-yaw-min/max, body-pitch-min/max, body-roll-min/max on the full body. Body roll is an AI edit by default (legs stay planted); set `roll_mode` = rotate for a rigid rotation about the hips.
eyes-closed, eyes-smile, mouth-a, mouth-i, mouth-u, mouth-e, mouth-o, brows-angry, brows-sad

## 6 · Connection targets
Hidden overlap art the PSD needs so nothing gaps at maximum motion: hair roots/back hair, jaw/neck, neck/collar/shoulders, sleeves/arms, waist/skirt/thighs, thighs/lower legs. Each panel is cropped to its body band. Use these as painting references for layers See-through could not complete.
eyes-closed, eyes-smile, mouth-a, mouth-i, mouth-u, mouth-e, mouth-o, brows-angry, brows-sad

## 7 · Expressions & visemes
Blink, smile-eyes, A/I/U/E/O mouths and brows on the face close-up. SAM3 isolates the changed region (eyes / mouth / eyebrows) and `StandRig Variant Layers` pastes each one back on the source canvas as a **hidden PSD layer** under `Variants/Expressions/…`, ready for StandRig opacity keys and viseme presets.
eyes-closed, eyes-smile, mouth-a, mouth-i, mouth-u, mouth-e, mouth-o, brows-angry, brows-sad

## 8 · Turnaround sheet (Multiple-Angles LoRA)
8 views around the character with the fal Multiple-Angles LoRA (`<sks> front-left quarter view …`). Use it as an orientation reference for back hair, accessories and body depth. Not part of the StandRig gate, but saved into the reference pack.
eyes-closed, eyes-smile, mouth-a, mouth-i, mouth-u, mouth-e, mouth-o, brows-angry, brows-sad
nodes.title: Prompts · turnaround_multiangle_lora

widgets_values:
## 9 · Part separation → PSD
See-through (SIGGRAPH 2026) decomposes the source canvas into up to 24 semantic layers **with the hidden parts painted in** (face under the bangs, back hair, eye whites…) and orders them by depth.

`StandRig Layers To PSD` maps them back to the source canvas, renames tags (hairf → Front Hair, eyewhite-l → Eye White L; L/R = character's own side), adds the expression variants as hidden layers and writes `output/standrig/<project>/<name>.psd` with ag-psd-compatible folders.

Needs the custom node pack **ComfyUI-See-through** (models auto-download from Hugging Face, ~16 GB VRAM at 1280; use nf4 / group_offload for 8–12 GB).

## 10 · Save the StandRig reference pack
Writes to `output/standrig/<project>/references/`:
`face-target.png`, `body-target.png`, `connection-target.png`, `expression-sheet.png`, `turnaround-sheet.png`, per-panel PNGs and **reference-manifest.json** (`standrig-visual-reference-v1`, sha256 of every image and of the PSD).

After importing the PSD in StandRig run `tools/pin_manifest.py` (or the *Pin Manifest* node) to pin the model revision, then hand the folder to your AI client.
